title: London cop shot with a crossbow during confrontation that led to man being gunned down by police
subtitle: The fatal shooting occurred during a raid at a house where police once seized a large weapons cache, including four loaded guns and 13,000 rounds of ammunition
article: A London police officer was shot with a crossbow during a confrontation that led to the shooting death of a man Friday morning, sources say.
The province's police watchdog is investigating the situation and has confirmed one officer was injured during the confrontation that led to the fatal shooting.
Paramedics were at the scene but did not transport anyone to hospital, said Middlesex London EMS duty manager Steve Cook.
He did not have details on the injured officer, who is believed to be part of the London police emergency response unit.
Sources have told The Free Press that the fatal shooting occurred after officers went to 56 Duchess Ave. to arrest someone around 6 a.m. Friday.
Neighbours report seeing officers in tactical gear around the home, which was occupied by a young family and has been the site of past weapons investigations.
At the address, somebody shot an officer with a crossbow. A man, age 35, was then shot and killed.
In 2007, police raided 56 Duchess Ave. and seized a large weapons cache, including four loaded guns and 13,000 rounds of ammunition.
Back then, police said the weapons were legally registered but not properly stored. Samuel Maloney, then 26, was charged with five counts of unsafe storage of a firearm and ammunition.
Neighbours say a couple and two young children, a baby and toddler, live at the red brick, single-storey house where the man was killed. The family moved into the red-brick house around 10 years ago.
One neighbour said she woke up to see more than a dozen tactical officers surrounding the house.
"They moved like a tank," said the neighbour, who didn't want to be identified.
The neighbour said she later saw the woman who lives at the house holding her toddler while being escorted by a police officer carrying baby from the home.
London police aren't releasing any additional information, citing the ongoing SIU probe.
The SIU, which has the power to lay criminal charges, investigates all cases of civilian death or serious injury involving police.
The 2007 seizure came after Canada Border Service Agency officers tipped off London police about a couple they arrested trying to bring 22 banned, high-capacity ammunition magazines into Windsor.
Melissa Facciolo, then 25, was charged with smuggling prohibited goods.
